overview: Nauru is a tiny island country in the central Pacific and the smallest republic in the world. It has no official capital; government offices are in the district of Yaren. Nauru became independent in 1968. It grew rich from mining phosphate, but most of the phosphate has now been dug up.

geography.text: Nauru is a single raised coral island, ringed by a reef and a narrow coastal strip where most people live. The central plateau, called Topside, was mined for phosphate for decades, leaving a landscape of jagged limestone pinnacles where little can grow.
